clue.text: Delight in birdsong when crossing height

indicators.note: one thing crossing another lies across it, so the birdsong word straddles the letter for height

parts.note: a trill is a warbling run of notes in a bird's song
H is the standard abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in hearing a bird sing as they walk over a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes in after the T of TRILL to give THRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to thrill is to give someone a sudden surge of pleasure, a close synonym.

clue.text: Takings from assembly room picked up

indicators.note: a sound picked up is one heard, as on a radio, so the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a hall is a room where people assemble

explanation.surface: Money collected at a village-hall event is gathered up at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A haul is a quantity of things taken, such as loot or a day's earnings, so it matches takings.

clue.text: Undergoing trial with a company's banks when will's lacking

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the state the noun names

parts.note: to be in something is to be undergoing it
a test is a trial
taken as written

indicators.note: a river's banks are its two edges, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of company

explanation.surface: A firm on trial, with its bankers involved, while a will is missing: a muddle of law and finance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like the financial institutions, but it means the outside letters of company.
explanation.definitionFit: Intestacy is the legal condition of dying without having made a valid will.

clue.text: Spooner's small Scottish song room

indicators.note: Dr Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words

parts.note: wee is Scots for small; its opening sound is traded
a lay is a ballad or song; its opening sound is traded

explanation.surface: The good doctor fumbles a request for a little Scottish tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the W and L of WEE LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom of movement or margin for action, which is what 'room' means in 'room to manoeuvre'.

clue.text: Second small cap went astray again

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
S is the abbreviation for small
a cap or lid covers a container

explanation.surface: A spare small cap rolled away and was lost a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal or a unit of time, but it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to relapse into bad ways after improving, so the past tense means strayed from virtue once more.

clue.text: Bone and short cartilage injured where beds arranged for visitors

indicators.note: something short lacks its end, so the final letter of the following word goes
injured things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A medical note of bone and cartilage damage, where hospital beds are set out for visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beds' suggests a hospital ward to match the injuries, but these are flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical garden is a public garden where plant beds are laid out for people to come and see.

clue.text: Entertainer's trick taking in reporters etc

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the trick word surrounds the other

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
the media covers reporters and other journalists, hence 'etc'

explanation.surface: A performer's stunt fools the press and their colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a performer who entertains audiences by making them laugh.

clue.text: Head's row overheard

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by ear, so the word counts by its sound

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat with oars

explanation.surface: A headteacher's argument is heard by others by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel, but it is the boating verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull is the bony case of the head, so it stands for head by close association.

clue.text: Reckless trendy individual turning tail

indicators.note: only the tail is turned round, so just the last two letters of the second word swap order

parts.note: in means fashionable
discrete means separate or individual

explanation.surface: A fashionable but careless person flees.
explanation.walkthrough: DISCRETE and DISCREET differ only in the order of their last two letters, which is the turned tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indiscreet means speaking or acting without care for consequences, a sense near enough to reckless.

clue.text: Solution obtained by division not quite working

indicators.note: letters that are working are being set in motion and reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A long-division sum gives an answer that is nearly but not quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, the quotient is the result produced when one number is divided by another.

clue.text: Blighted cast close to mutiny

parts.note: a cast is a mould for shaping metal or plaster

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of mutiny

explanation.surface: A crew on the brink of revolt, its doomed actors cast in a failing production.
explanation.definitionFit: Blight and mould are both fungal plant diseases, so something mouldy is spoiled or blighted.

clue.text: Spotted girl going round grand cathedral's colourful display?

indicators.note: the two-word phrase goes round, enclosing the abbreviation between its words

parts.note: something stained is marked with spots
lass is a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A girl with a spotty face is touring a grand cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' applies to the whole two-word phrase, so G lands at the gap between its words; G for grand is a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathedral windows of coloured glass make a bright display, an example rather than a synonym, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Movie-maker's constant echo penetrating behind closed doors

parts.note: c is the symbol for the constant speed of light

indicators.note: a thing penetrating another goes inside it, so one letter is pushed into the phrase

parts.note: in camera is the legal phrase for proceedings held in private
Echo is the radio code word for E

explanation.surface: A film director keeps hearing a persistent echo that gets into a private meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind closed doors' is the Latin legal term used for court hearings closed to the public; the echo letter slips between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cine camera is a device for shooting moving film, so it literally makes movies.

clue.text: Leading lady starts to dominate in vaudeville act

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: The star of a variety show begins to take over the act.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female singer, the leading lady of an opera company.

clue.text: Moves awkwardly and clears off, hampering doctor

indicators.note: to hamper is to hem in, so the rearranged letters close round the doctor
off means gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles and runs off, getting in a doctor's way.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamber is to climb or move clumsily using hands and feet.

clue.text: Ex-PM put up with fearsome Eurasian

parts.note: Gordon Brown was UK Prime Minister from 2007 to 2010
to bear something is to put up with it

explanation.surface: A former prime minister tolerated a frightening foreign statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eurasian' reads as a person, but it is an animal native to Europe and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The brown bear is a large, dangerous species found across Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Underrate French peach, one dry inside

indicators.note: the last two items sit inside the French word, placed within it

parts.note: belle is French for a beauty, and a peach is an attractive woman
I is the Roman numeral one
TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone undervalues a French peach because one of them is dry in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peach' suggests fruit, but here it is a lovely woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle is to make something seem less important than it is, so to underrate it.

clue.text: Thriving, or just OK?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in very good health
second meaning: a grudging 'all right then'

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase serves as high praise and as a reluctant agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense describes someone in excellent health; the other is a resigned phrase of consent like 'fine'.

clue.text: Outstanding poetry recital

indicators.note: a recital is a spoken performance, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A brilliant performance of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise, but it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still owed, not yet settled.

clue.text: Jewish people accepting Roman Catholic gem

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the people word surrounds the church

parts.note: Zion can stand for the Jewish people as a whole
RC is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An interfaith picture of Jews welcoming a Catholic who is a gem of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Zircon is a mineral cut as a gemstone, often as a diamond substitute.

clue.text: Consequence of sheep's sex change procedure?

parts.note: surface reading: an operation to change a sheep's sex
setter's reading: turning a ewe into a male sheep, treated as a made-up process noun built on the word for a male sheep

explanation.surface: An outcome of giving a sheep gender reassignment surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as RAM-IFICATION, the 'making into a ram' of a ewe; the question mark flags the invented sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramification is a result or knock-on effect of an action, often unwelcome.

clue.text: Bumbling in record time

parts.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles while setting a fast lap time.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumbling describes clumsy, incompetent behaviour, which is what inept means.

clue.text: Foul lifts not recorded

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word raises it from bottom to top so it reads upwards

parts.note: foul and evil both mean wicked

explanation.surface: A spoken warning that broken lifts are not caught on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifts' reads as elevators, but it is the instruction to turn the word upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A live broadcast is transmitted as it happens rather than prerecorded.

clue.text: Minimal payments covering women's toilets at first

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap it, so the payments word wraps round the letter for women

parts.note: fees are payments for services
W is the abbreviation for women, as on a toilet door

indicators.note: first means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of toilets

explanation.surface: Charges for the ladies' toilets were kept very low at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Fewest means the smallest number, which is minimal.

clue.text: Doddering engineers on retiring list after last month

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the last month of the year
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: something retiring draws back, so the word for list is read backwards

parts.note: a ship that lists tips or leans to one side

explanation.surface: Elderly engineers are put on the retired list after December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' reads as a register of names, but it is the verb for leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means worn out and feeble with age, just as a doddering person is shaky and frail.

clue.text: Temple of Greek god, old parts in addition

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild

indicators.note: to part something is to split it, so the letter for old pushes into the following phrase

parts.note: then can mean also or besides
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A shrine to a Greek god with ancient sections added on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is a temple dedicated to all the gods, most famously the one in Rome.

clue.text: Annoyed when raven's last aboard Noah's craft

indicators.note: the last of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of raven
a playful verb: put on board the Ark, as if 'arked'

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the raven was the final creature to board the Ark.
explanation.walkthrough: N is placed before ARKED, a made-up past tense for being taken onto Noah's Ark. Narked is British slang for irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Narked is informal British slang meaning irritated or annoyed.
